headline: MOONSHOT CANCELS
**$150M** CHIP DEAL
cover.hook_pick_reason: The $150M cancellation is the concrete, named event and slide 2 states it in full, with 'reportedly' carried on every slide. The claim hook (US limits reach the cloud) is the broader angle but is our framing of a single report, so it is less safe. The third hook is accurate but weaker than the first. slides.title: Moonshot AI pulls out
body: Moonshot AI, the Chinese startup behind the Kimi models, **reportedly** cancelled a **$150M** (about ₩200B) deal to rent Nvidia's latest AI chips through an Indonesian data center, per The Information, as relayed by Korea's AI Times.

slides.title: Half up front, reportedly
body: The deal was for Nvidia's Blackwell Ultra B300 chips from a Southeast Asian **neocloud**, a company that rents out AI chips in the cloud. Moonshot had reportedly agreed to pay **50%** up front. About 15% is usual.

slides.title: A new US rule
body: The reported trigger is a US Commerce Department rule announced Nov 16 and in force from Nov 19. Overseas data centers serving Chinese customers above a certain size need **US government permission**.

slides.title: 90 days to get a licence
body: Data centers already serving Chinese firms above that size must get a US licence within **90 days**. The threshold is compute equal to about **300** of the latest AI chips, AI Times writes.

slides.title: Other talks are paused
body: Moonshot has also reportedly paused talks on other new GPU rental deals while it reviews the rule's impact. It was seeking more GPUs for its next model, Kimi K4. Its K3, out in July, drew notice for performance comparable to major US models.

facts.text: Moonshot AI cancelled a deal worth $150 million (about 200 billion won) to rent Nvidia's latest AI chips through an Indonesian data center. 'Chinese startup behind the Kimi models' is the writer's explainer.

The Information reported on the 19th (US time), citing multiple sources, that Moonshot withdrew from a Blackwell Ultra B300 rental deal with a Southeast Asian neocloud company. 'Neocloud' is glossed as a company that rents out AI chips in the cloud.
Moonshot had reportedly accepted paying 50% of the contract up front; the usual prepayment ratio is about 15%.
The trigger is a new US Commerce Department rule announced on the 16th and in force from the 19th (month Nov inferred from the article date, Nov 20, 2026).
The rule requires overseas data centers serving Chinese customers above a certain size to get US government permission.
Data centers already serving Chinese firms above that size must get a US licence within 90 days; the threshold is compute equal to about 300 of the latest AI chips.
Moonshot has also paused negotiations on other new GPU rental deals while it reviews the rule's impact.
Moonshot's K3 model, released in July, drew attention for performance comparable to major US models; the company was seeking more GPUs for its next model, Kimi K4.

sources.title_en: Moonshot AI cancels Nvidia chip rental deal worth 200 billion won over US export controls

caption:
Moonshot AI reportedly cancelled a $150M Nvidia chip rental in Indonesia after a new US rule.

This is a single-source report: Korea's AI Times cites The Information, and we have not seen comment from Moonshot or Nvidia. Moonshot is the Chinese startup behind the Kimi models. The rule covers overseas data centers that serve Chinese customers, so renting chips in a third country is now caught too.

→ Reportedly a $150M (about ₩200B) rental of Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 chips, with 50% to be paid up front
→ US Commerce Department rule in force from Nov 19: big overseas data centers serving Chinese customers need US permission, and existing ones have 90 days to get a licence
→ Moonshot has also paused talks on other GPU rentals while it reviews the rule

Is renting chips abroad still a way around export controls?

Source: AI Times (Korea), "Moonshot AI cancels Nvidia chip rental deal worth 200 billion won over US export controls" (in Korean), Nov 20, 2026.
